text: APT28 (Fancy Bear) is a Russian state-sponsored threat group attributed to the GRU Unit 26165. Active since at least 2004, the group targets government, military, and security organizations primarily in NATO countries. Known for exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in VPN appliances and using custom tooling including X-Agent, XTunnel, and Zebrocy for espionage operations.

APT29 (Cozy Bear) is a Russian espionage group attributed to the SVR foreign intelligence service. Gained significant notoriety for the 2020 SolarWinds supply chain compromise. The group demonstrates exceptional operational security, leveraging legitimate cloud services for C2, using residential proxies, and maintaining long-term persistent access with minimal indicators.

Lazarus Group is a North Korean state-sponsored threat actor attributed to the Reconnaissance General Bureau. The group conducts both espionage and financially motivated operations, including cryptocurrency theft totaling billions of dollars. Known campaigns include the Sony Pictures hack (2014), WannaCry ransomware (2017), and the Ronin Bridge cryptocurrency theft of $620M (2022).

FIN7 (Carbanak Group) is a financially motivated threat group that has stolen over $1 billion from banks and retail organizations worldwide. The group has evolved from POS malware attacks to ransomware operations, maintaining affiliations with ALPHV/BlackCat and other RaaS programs. FIN7 uses sophisticated social engineering and operates fake penetration testing companies to recruit unwitting developers.

LockBit ransomware operation was the most prolific RaaS (Ransomware-as-a-Service) program from 2021-2024, responsible for over 1,700 known attacks globally. Despite the February 2024 Operation Cronos disruption by law enforcement, remnants of the operation attempted reconstitution. The group pioneered bug bounty programs for their malware and used triple extortion tactics including DDoS threats.

ALPHV/BlackCat was a sophisticated ransomware operation written in Rust, active from November 2021 through early 2024. Notable for cross-platform capabilities targeting Windows, Linux, and VMware ESXi. The group conducted a high-profile attack against MGM Resorts in collaboration with Scattered Spider, demonstrating the convergence of social engineering and ransomware deployment tactics.

Scattered Spider (UNC3944/Octo Tempest) is an English-speaking threat group known for sophisticated social engineering and SIM swapping attacks. The group targets identity providers and help desks to gain initial access, then deploys ransomware through RaaS partnerships. Members are predominantly young adults operating from the US and UK, distinguishing them from traditional nation-state adversaries.

Analysis of the Midnight Blizzard campaign targeting Microsoft 365 environments through OAuth application abuse. The campaign leveraged compromised small business tenants to create malicious OAuth applications, which were then used to access email accounts across targeted organizations. The attack demonstrated the risk of federated trust relationships in cloud environments.

Deep dive analysis of CVE-2024-3400, a critical command injection vulnerability (CVSS 10.0) in Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect VPN gateway. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution via specially crafted HTTP requests to the device management interface. Active exploitation by UTA0218 was observed before patch availability, with attackers deploying Python-based backdoors.

Analysis of CVE-2024-1709, a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in ConnectWise ScreenConnect. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to create administrative accounts on the ScreenConnect server, leading to full system compromise. Multiple ransomware groups including LockBit and PLAY actively exploited this vulnerability within 48 hours of disclosure.

Campaign analysis of Volt Typhoon (Bronze Silhouette) pre-positioning operations in US critical infrastructure. The Chinese state-sponsored group exclusively uses living-off-the-land techniques, avoiding custom malware to evade detection. Focus areas include water treatment, energy, and telecommunications. Persistence is maintained through compromised SOHO routers forming a KV-botnet proxy network.

Industry report on the healthcare sector threat landscape for 2024-2025. Healthcare organizations experienced a 72% increase in ransomware attacks, with average ransom demands exceeding $1.5M. Key attack vectors include exploitation of unpatched VPN appliances, compromised credentials from infostealers, and exploitation of legacy medical devices running unsupported operating systems.

Technical analysis of the T1059.001 (PowerShell) technique across observed intrusions. PowerShell remains the most frequently abused living-off-the-land binary, used in 68% of Windows-based intrusions. Analysis covers obfuscation methods including Invoke-Obfuscation, AMSI bypass techniques, constrained language mode evasion, and detection strategies using ScriptBlock logging and ETW tracing.

Analysis of CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887, a chained authentication bypass and command injection vulnerability in Ivanti Connect Secure VPN. Exploited by multiple threat actors including UNC5221, who deployed custom malware families BUSHWALK and LIGHTWIRE for persistence. The vulnerabilities affected thousands of organizations globally due to slow patch adoption.

Sandworm (APT44) profile covering the Russian GRU Unit 74455 threat group responsible for some of the most destructive cyberattacks in history including NotPetya, Olympic Destroyer, and multiple attacks on Ukrainian critical infrastructure. The group has evolved to conduct both destructive operations and espionage, increasingly targeting operational technology environments.

Campaign analysis of the MOVEit Transfer mass exploitation campaign attributed to Clop ransomware group. CVE-2023-34362 SQL injection vulnerability was exploited to deploy the LEMURLOOT web shell across thousands of MOVEit instances. Over 2,500 organizations were affected with data theft impacting over 80 million individuals, making it one of the largest data breaches in history.

Technical deep dive into T1556.006 (Multi-Factor Authentication Bypass) techniques observed in the wild. Covers adversary-in-the-middle frameworks (EvilGinx2, Modlishka), MFA fatigue/push bombing, SIM swapping for SMS OTP interception, and abuse of FIDO2 device binding gaps. Includes detection opportunities at each stage.

Industry report on the financial sector cyber threat landscape. Key findings include a 45% increase in attacks targeting SWIFT messaging infrastructure, emergence of AI-powered vishing campaigns targeting wealth management clients, and growing exploitation of open banking APIs. Average cost of a financial sector breach reached $6.1M in 2024.

CVE-2024-37085 analysis covering the VMware ESXi Active Directory integration vulnerability. The flaw allows attackers who can create an AD group named 'ESX Admins' to gain full administrative access to ESXi hypervisors. Exploited by multiple ransomware groups including ALPHV/BlackCat and Akira to encrypt virtual machine disk files directly on the hypervisor.

Analysis of the Akira ransomware group, active since March 2023 and responsible for over 250 attacks primarily targeting small and medium businesses. Akira exploits VPN vulnerabilities (particularly Cisco ASA CVE-2023-20269) for initial access and has both Windows and Linux/ESXi encryptors. The group is believed to have connections to the former Conti ransomware operation.

Technical analysis of T1003 (OS Credential Dumping) sub-techniques observed across 500 incident response engagements. LSASS memory dumping via comsvcs.dll MiniDump remains the most common method (42%), followed by ntds.dit extraction (28%), and SAM registry hive extraction (15%). Credential Guard and PPL enforcement significantly reduce successful exploitation.

Campaign analysis of the Star Blizzard (formerly SEABORGIUM) spear-phishing operation targeting think tanks and academics. The Russian FSB-linked group creates elaborate personas on social media, builds rapport over weeks, then delivers credential harvesting links via shared documents. Campaigns specifically target researchers working on Russia-Ukraine policy issues.

CVE-2024-4577 analysis covering the critical PHP-CGI argument injection vulnerability affecting Windows PHP installations. CVSS 9.8, the flaw exploits a character encoding handling issue in Windows Best-Fit mapping to inject command-line arguments to the PHP binary. Widespread exploitation observed within 24 hours of PoC publication, primarily for webshell deployment and cryptominer installation.

Industry report on the manufacturing sector cyber threat landscape. Manufacturing surpassed financial services as the most targeted industry in 2024. Key threats include ransomware attacks targeting OT/ICS systems, intellectual property theft by Chinese APT groups, and exploitation of internet-exposed HMI and SCADA systems. Average downtime from manufacturing ransomware incidents reached 12 days.

Turla (Snake/Venomous Bear) actor profile covering the FSB Center 16 group known for highly sophisticated espionage operations. Turla maintains one of the most advanced toolkits among nation-state actors, including the ComRAT v4 backdoor using the Gmail API for C2 and the LightNeuron backdoor targeting Microsoft Exchange servers for email interception.

Technical analysis of T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) trends across 2024-2025. Edge devices (VPNs, firewalls, load balancers) became the primary initial access vector, displacing phishing for the first time. Ivanti, Palo Alto, Fortinet, and Citrix products accounted for 78% of exploited edge vulnerabilities. Analysis includes detection strategies using NetFlow and application-level monitoring.

Campaign analysis of the Chinese APT group Salt Typhoon (GhostEmperor) targeting telecommunications providers. The group compromised call detail record systems at major US telecom carriers, enabling surveillance of targeted individuals. The operation leveraged custom rootkits and exploited Cisco IOS XE vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-20198) for initial access to network infrastructure.

CVE-2025-0282 analysis covering the Ivanti Connect Secure stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability. Pre-authentication remote code execution with CVSS 9.0. Exploited by UNC5337 to deploy the SPAWN malware ecosystem (SPAWNANT, SPAWNMOLE, SPAWNSNAIL) for persistent access. The vulnerability highlights the continued targeting of VPN edge devices as a preferred initial access vector.

Profile of the BianLian ransomware group that shifted from data encryption to pure data extortion in 2024. The group exploits ProxyShell and exposed RDP for initial access, uses ngrok and Rclone for data exfiltration, and pressures victims through public leak sites. BianLian has particularly targeted healthcare and legal services organizations.

Industry report on the education sector cyber threat landscape. Universities and K-12 institutions experienced a 105% increase in ransomware attacks in 2024. Key challenges include legacy systems, limited security budgets, and large attack surfaces from BYOD policies. Akira and LockBit were the most active ransomware groups targeting the sector.

Technical analysis of T1021.002 (SMB/Windows Admin Shares) for lateral movement. Covers common tools used including PsExec, Impacket smbexec/wmiexec, and CrackMapExec. Detection opportunities include monitoring for named pipe creation, anomalous service installations, and remote file writes to ADMIN$ shares. Includes SIEM correlation rules for Splunk and Microsoft Sentinel.

Campaign analysis of the MuddyWater (MERCURY) operations targeting Middle Eastern organizations. The Iranian MOIS-linked group has expanded operations to include destructive wiper attacks alongside traditional espionage. The group uses legitimate RMM tools including Atera and SimpleHelp for persistence, and MuddyC2Go for C2 communication.

CVE-2024-21762 analysis covering the Fortinet FortiOS out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the SSL VPN daemon. CVSS 9.6, exploited in the wild before disclosure. Allows unauthenticated remote code execution via specially crafted HTTP requests. Over 150,000 FortiGate devices were exposed to the internet at the time of disclosure, with mass exploitation beginning within days.

Profile of Rhysida ransomware group active since May 2023, notable for targeting government institutions, healthcare, and education. The group operates a RaaS model and was responsible for the British Library attack. Rhysida uses phishing and exploits Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) for privilege escalation, deploying ransomware via PsExec and Group Policy Objects.

Technical analysis of T1562.001 (Disable or Modify Tools) covering EDR evasion techniques. Includes analysis of Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attacks using drivers like truesight.sys and gmer.sys, direct kernel object manipulation (DKOM), and abuse of Windows Defender exclusion paths. Recommends driver block list enforcement and tamper protection monitoring.

Campaign analysis of the XZ Utils supply chain compromise (CVE-2024-3094). A sophisticated multi-year social engineering operation where a contributor inserted a backdoor into the xz compression library targeting OpenSSH authentication. The backdoor would have enabled unauthorized access to millions of Linux systems. Discovered accidentally by a Microsoft developer who noticed SSH latency anomalies.

CVE-2024-47575 analysis covering the FortiManager unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability (FortiJump). CVSS 9.8, the flaw in the FGFM protocol allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands on FortiManager instances. UNC5820 exploited the vulnerability to exfiltrate managed FortiGate configuration data including hashed passwords and policy rules.

Industry report on the energy sector cyber threat landscape. ICS/SCADA attacks increased 87% year-over-year with particular focus on power grid operations and natural gas pipeline systems. Key threat actors include Sandworm, Volt Typhoon, and CyberAv3ngers (Iranian). Recommendations include OT network segmentation, Purdue model enforcement, and passive monitoring solutions.

Technical analysis of T1567 (Exfiltration Over Web Service) covering attacker abuse of legitimate cloud storage services for data exfiltration. Analysis of Rclone, MEGACmd, and custom tools using Google Drive, OneDrive, and Dropbox APIs. Detection strategies include monitoring for unusual cloud storage uploads, DLP integration, and DNS-based indicators for file-sharing services.

Profile of Kimsuky (Velvet Chollima) North Korean threat group primarily conducting espionage against South Korean government, think tanks, and academic institutions. The group uses spear-phishing with malicious HWP documents, credential harvesting via fake login portals, and custom malware families including BabyShark and AppleSeed. Increasingly targeting the cryptocurrency and blockchain industry.

Wizard Spider is a Russia-based financially motivated threat group responsible for the Trickbot banking trojan, Ryuk ransomware, and Conti ransomware operations. Following the Conti dissolution in 2022, members splintered into multiple successor groups including Royal/BlackSuit, Akira, and Zeon. The group pioneered the big game hunting ransomware model, targeting high-revenue organizations for maximum extortion payouts.

Evil Corp (Indrik Spider) is a Russian cybercriminal organization led by Maksim Yakubets, responsible for the Dridex banking trojan and BitPaymer/WastedLocker/Hades ransomware families. Sanctioned by OFAC in 2019, the group has repeatedly rebranded its ransomware to help victims circumvent sanctions restrictions on ransom payments. Known connections to Russian intelligence services complicate the criminal-state nexus.

FIN8 (Syssphinx) is a financially motivated threat group active since at least 2016, initially targeting point-of-sale systems in the hospitality and retail sectors. The group evolved to deploy the White Rabbit and Sardonic backdoor, and has been observed deploying ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware in recent campaigns. FIN8 uses living-off-the-land techniques and custom PowerShell scripts for persistence.

FIN12 (Pistol Tempest) is a ransomware-focused threat actor notable for skipping the data exfiltration step, proceeding directly to encryption to minimize dwell time. The group relies on initial access brokers for entry and has deployed Ryuk, Conti, Hive, and BlackCat ransomware. FIN12 has disproportionately targeted healthcare organizations, with average time-to-ransom under 48 hours.

TA505 is a prolific financially motivated threat group responsible for distributing Dridex, Locky ransomware, and the FlawedAmmyy RAT through massive spam campaigns. The group operates the Clop ransomware and has conducted some of the largest mass exploitation campaigns in history, including the MOVEit, GoAnywhere, and Accellion FTA attacks. TA505 targets managed file transfer solutions for maximum impact.

TA577 is a prolific initial access broker distributing QakBot (Qbot) and Pikabot malware through email campaigns. The group uses thread hijacking, HTML smuggling, and password-protected ZIP archives to bypass email security gateways. TA577 sells network access to ransomware affiliates, serving as a critical link in the ransomware supply chain ecosystem.

Ember Bear (Cadet Blizzard/DEV-0586) is a Russian GRU-linked threat group responsible for the WhisperGate destructive malware deployed against Ukrainian government networks in January 2022. The group masquerades destructive operations as ransomware, uses commodity tools for initial access, and targets government and critical infrastructure in Ukraine and NATO member states supporting Ukraine.

Detailed analysis of Midnight Blizzard (APT29) tradecraft evolution in 2024-2025. The group expanded OAuth abuse to include creation of malicious Entra ID applications for email harvesting, leveraged Azure AD certificate-based authentication for persistence, and compromised Microsoft corporate email to access customer environments. The campaign highlights the risk of trusted vendor compromise.

UNC3886 is a Chinese espionage group targeting networking, virtualization, and edge devices with zero-day exploits. The group exploited VMware vCenter (CVE-2023-34048) and Fortinet FortiOS vulnerabilities to deploy custom backdoors on ESXi hypervisors and network appliances. UNC3886 specifically targets devices that lack EDR coverage, demonstrating deep understanding of enterprise security blind spots.

UNC2452 (Dark Halo) is the threat cluster responsible for the SolarWinds Orion supply chain compromise discovered in December 2020. The group demonstrated exceptional tradecraft by limiting Sunburst backdoor deployment to select targets, using unique indicators per victim, and maintaining operational security that evaded detection for over 9 months. Attributed to Russia SVR and merged into APT29 tracking.

Deep dive into living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) abuse across 2024-2025 intrusions. The top 10 abused LOLBins include certutil.exe for file downloads, mshta.exe for HTA script execution, rundll32.exe for DLL proxy execution, regsvr32.exe for COM scriptlet execution, and wmic.exe for remote execution. Analysis covers detection strategies including command-line argument monitoring, parent-child process analysis, and baseline deviation alerting.

Technical analysis of AMSI (Antimalware Scan Interface) bypass techniques used by threat actors to evade PowerShell and .NET-based detections. Covers amsi.dll patching via reflective loading, AmsiScanBuffer function hooking, PowerShell CLM bypass through InstallUtil and MSBuild, and AMSI provider hijacking via registry modification. Detection recommendations include ETW monitoring and integrity verification of amsi.dll in memory.

Comprehensive analysis of EDR evasion techniques observed across 300 incident response engagements. Primary methods include BYOVD attacks (34%), userland API unhooking via direct syscalls (22%), ETW patching to blind telemetry (18%), and DLL side-loading into EDR-excluded processes (15%). Emerging techniques include abuse of Windows Filtering Platform to block EDR network communications and kernel callback removal.

Technical deep dive into cloud attack paths targeting Azure Active Directory (Entra ID). Covers token theft via device code phishing, consent grant attacks for OAuth application permissions, Azure AD Connect credential extraction, Primary Refresh Token abuse for lateral movement, and exploitation of managed identity tokens from compromised VMs. Includes detection queries for Microsoft Sentinel and Defender for Cloud.

Analysis of AWS IAM attack paths commonly exploited in cloud breaches. Covers exploitation of overly permissive IAM policies, role chaining for privilege escalation, SSRF attacks against the EC2 metadata service (IMDSv1), Lambda function credential harvesting, and abuse of cross-account assume-role trust relationships. Includes Pacu and Prowler-based detection methodologies and CloudTrail log analysis techniques.

Technical analysis of container escape techniques targeting Kubernetes and Docker environments. Covers privileged container breakout via /proc/self/exe, exploitation of CVE-2024-21626 (runc Leaky Vessels), host filesystem mount abuse, Kubernetes API server exploitation via exposed service accounts, and abuse of hostPID/hostNetwork namespaces. Includes runtime security detection with Falco and Tracee.

Comprehensive guide to Active Directory attack chains using modern offensive tooling. Covers BloodHound for attack path enumeration, Rubeus for Kerberos abuse including AS-REP roasting and constrained delegation attacks, Certifried (CVE-2022-26923) for AD CS certificate-based privilege escalation, and Shadow Credentials attacks via msDS-KeyCredentialLink. Includes defensive recommendations for each attack stage.

Industry threat landscape report for the energy and utilities sector covering 2024-2025. Key findings include increased targeting of smart grid infrastructure by state-sponsored actors, exploitation of OPC UA protocol vulnerabilities in industrial environments, and emergence of ransomware groups specifically targeting operational technology. The Sandworm-attributed attacks on Ukrainian power grid substations serve as case studies for potential attack playbooks against Western utilities.

Industry threat landscape report for the retail and e-commerce sector. Major threats include Magecart-style skimming attacks injecting malicious JavaScript into payment pages, credential stuffing attacks against customer accounts using stealer log credentials, and ransomware targeting peak shopping periods for maximum leverage. Supply chain compromise of e-commerce plugins and payment gateway integrations emerged as a growing concern.

Industry threat landscape report for the telecommunications sector covering 2024-2025. Telecom providers face persistent threats from Chinese state-sponsored groups (Salt Typhoon, Volt Typhoon) targeting call detail records and lawful intercept systems. SS7 protocol exploitation, SIM swapping operations, and BGP hijacking continue to threaten network infrastructure. The sector saw a 63% increase in attacks on 5G core network components.

Industry threat landscape report for the government and public sector. Government agencies at all levels experienced a 90% increase in ransomware attacks, with particular impact on municipal services and law enforcement. State-sponsored espionage targeting classified systems intensified, with APT29 and APT28 focusing on diplomatic communications. Insider threat incidents involving access to sensitive databases rose significantly.

Industry threat landscape report for the legal services sector. Law firms are increasingly targeted for privileged attorney-client communications, merger and acquisition intelligence, and intellectual property. BianLian and ALPHV ransomware groups specifically targeted large law firms in 2024. Business email compromise attacks impersonating partners to redirect client trust account disbursements resulted in losses exceeding $400M sector-wide.

Industry threat landscape report for the transportation and logistics sector. Attacks against shipping, aviation, and rail systems increased 78% year-over-year. Key incidents include ransomware attacks disrupting port operations, GPS spoofing affecting maritime navigation, and cyber attacks on railway signaling systems. The convergence of IT and OT systems in modern transportation infrastructure creates expanded attack surfaces.

Post-incident analysis of Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) long-term impact assessment as of 2025. Despite three years since disclosure, approximately 12% of Java applications in enterprise environments remain vulnerable. Analysis covers persistent backdoors planted during the initial exploitation wave that remained undetected, reinfection via transitive dependencies, and ongoing exploitation by cryptocurrency miners and initial access brokers against forgotten Java services.

Comprehensive analysis of MOVEit Transfer exploitation aftermath and lessons learned. The Clop ransomware group's mass exploitation of CVE-2023-34362 affected over 2,600 organizations and 84 million individuals. Analysis covers the total economic impact exceeding $10 billion, regulatory consequences including multiple GDPR enforcement actions, and the operational patterns that enabled Clop to prepare exploitation infrastructure months before disclosure.

Analysis of Citrix Bleed (CVE-2023-4966) exploitation and downstream impacts. The vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway allowed session token theft enabling authenticated access bypass. LockBit affiliates were the primary exploiters, using stolen session tokens to access internal networks of major corporations. Analysis covers detection of exploitation artifacts, session validation hardening, and the 60-day window between patch availability and mass exploitation.

Analysis of Fortinet VPN exploitation chains observed across 2024-2025, covering the sequential exploitation of CVE-2024-21762, CVE-2024-47575, CVE-2024-55591, and CVE-2025-24472. The cascading vulnerabilities in FortiOS and FortiManager demonstrate how a single vendor vulnerability disclosure can be followed by related discoveries. Covers the UNC5820 and Mora_001 threat clusters responsible for active exploitation.

Analysis of AI-powered cyber attacks emerging in 2024-2025. Threat actors are leveraging large language models to generate polymorphic malware that evades signature-based detection, create convincing spear-phishing emails at scale in multiple languages, and automate vulnerability discovery in open-source codebases. Criminal forums now offer AI-as-a-service for phishing content generation, voice cloning, and CAPTCHA solving.

Analysis of deepfake social engineering attacks targeting corporate executives and financial operations. Documented cases include AI-generated video conference participants authorizing fraudulent wire transfers totaling over $75M in 2024-2025. Attack patterns include cloning executive voices from earnings calls and public appearances, generating real-time video deepfakes for virtual meetings, and combining deepfakes with compromised email for multi-channel validation of fraudulent requests.

Analysis of LLM prompt injection attacks targeting enterprise AI deployments. Threat actors have discovered techniques to manipulate AI assistants integrated with corporate systems to exfiltrate sensitive data, bypass access controls through conversational manipulation, and execute unauthorized actions via tool-use capabilities. Attack vectors include indirect prompt injection through poisoned documents, emails, and web content that AI systems process on behalf of users.

Campaign analysis of Cadet Blizzard (DEV-0586) operations in 2024-2025 targeting NATO member state government networks. The group evolved from crude wiper deployments to more sophisticated data destruction operations disguised as ransomware. Analysis covers the group's use of stolen legitimate credentials from underground markets, exploitation of Exchange Server vulnerabilities, and coordination with Russian military operations timeline.

Technical deep dive into Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) attack paths. Covers ESC1 through ESC13 misconfiguration-based attacks documented by SpecterOps, including overly permissive certificate templates enabling domain privilege escalation, NTLM relay to AD CS web enrollment (PetitPotam), and abuse of Certificate Authority backup procedures. Tools covered include Certify, Certipy, and ForgeCert for golden certificate attacks.

Analysis of Kerberos abuse techniques in Active Directory environments covering AS-REP roasting, Kerberoasting, Silver Ticket attacks, Golden Ticket attacks, and Diamond Ticket attacks. Includes detailed coverage of Rubeus tool capabilities, detection strategies using Windows Event Log 4769 monitoring, and honeypot service account configurations for early warning of Kerberoasting activity.

Campaign analysis of UNC3886 exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities in VMware and Fortinet products throughout 2024. The Chinese espionage group demonstrated advanced understanding of hypervisor internals, deploying custom REPTILE and MEDUSA rootkits on ESXi hosts. The campaign targeted defense industrial base entities and telecommunications companies, with the group maintaining access for an average of 14 months before detection.

Analysis of BloodHound attack path enumeration in enterprise environments. Covers how threat actors use BloodHound and SharpHound to map Active Directory trust relationships, identify shortest paths to Domain Admin, discover Kerberos delegation vulnerabilities, and find Azure AD hybrid join misconfigurations. Defensive guidance includes running BloodHound proactively for attack path analysis, implementing tiered administration, and monitoring LDAP query anomalies.

Analysis of AI-generated phishing campaigns at scale observed in 2025. Threat actors leveraged language models to produce context-aware phishing emails personalized with scraped LinkedIn and social media data. The AI-generated content eliminated grammatical errors traditionally used as phishing indicators, and automated A/B testing of subject lines increased click-through rates by an estimated 300% compared to traditional templates.

Analysis of emerging AI model poisoning attacks targeting enterprise machine learning pipelines. Threat actors compromised public model repositories and training data sources to introduce subtle backdoors into ML models used for fraud detection, content moderation, and security classification. The poisoned models behaved normally under standard testing but produced attacker-desired outputs when presented with specific trigger patterns.

metadata.relevance: technology, financial, all industries deploying AI

text: Analysis of CVE-2024-6387 (regreSSHion) OpenSSH vulnerability impact assessment. The race condition in OpenSSH's SIGALRM signal handler allowed unauthenticated remote code execution on glibc-based Linux systems. Analysis covers the regression from CVE-2006-5051, exploitation difficulty in practice, affected distribution versions, and the global exposure of 14 million SSH servers. Successful exploitation requires 6-8 hours of sustained connections on average.

Profile of TA505 (Clop ransomware) mass exploitation methodology. The group systematically identifies and stockpiles zero-day vulnerabilities in file transfer appliances, preparing exploitation infrastructure before disclosure. Analysis of the Accellion FTA, GoAnywhere MFT, MOVEit Transfer, and Cleo exploitation campaigns reveals a consistent operational pattern including pre-staged web shells, automated data exfiltration, and staggered victim notification for maximum ransom collection.

Campaign analysis of Midnight Blizzard (APT29) targeting of cloud service providers and their customers in 2025. The group exploited trusted relationships between cloud providers and enterprise tenants, using stolen OAuth tokens and service principal credentials to access email, SharePoint, and Azure DevOps environments. The campaign underscored systemic risk in cloud supply chains and the difficulty of detecting abuse of legitimate authentication mechanisms.

Technical analysis of LOLBin abuse specifically targeting macOS environments. Covers abuse of osascript for AppleScript-based command execution, curl for payload download, open command for launching malicious applications, security command for keychain access, and dscl for local account manipulation. Includes detection strategies using Endpoint Security Framework telemetry and Unified Log analysis.

metadata.relevance: technology, creative industries, all macOS environments

text: Analysis of cloud-native attack chains targeting multi-cloud environments. Covers lateral movement between AWS, Azure, and GCP through federated identity trust, exploitation of workload identity federation, and abuse of Terraform state files containing cloud credentials. Includes case studies of real-world breaches where attackers pivoted from a development AWS account to production Azure environments through shared CI/CD infrastructure.

Profile of RansomHub ransomware-as-a-service operation that rapidly gained market share following the ALPHV/BlackCat exit scam and LockBit disruption. The group offers affiliates 90% revenue share and provides both Windows and Linux/ESXi encryptors written in Golang and C++. RansomHub specifically recruits experienced affiliates from disbanded operations and has targeted over 200 organizations across critical infrastructure sectors.

Analysis of deepfake video attacks in the enterprise authentication context. Threat actors have deployed real-time deepfake video to bypass KYC verification processes at financial institutions, defeat video-based identity proofing during remote onboarding, and impersonate executives in virtual board meetings. Analysis covers current deepfake detection limitations and recommends multi-modal verification including liveness detection and behavioral biometrics.

Analysis of indirect prompt injection attacks against enterprise RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems. Attackers embed malicious instructions within documents stored in corporate knowledge bases, which are then retrieved and executed by AI assistants when users query related topics. Demonstrated attack scenarios include data exfiltration through AI-generated responses, privilege escalation via AI tool-use capabilities, and social engineering through AI-mediated communications.

metadata.relevance: technology, all industries deploying AI assistants

text: Campaign analysis of Wizard Spider successor groups operating under the Conti diaspora. Former Conti members fragmented into at least five distinct operational clusters running Royal/BlackSuit, Akira, Zeon, Silent Ransom (Luna Moth), and Quantum ransomware. Analysis maps the organizational structure, shared infrastructure, and evolved TTPs across these successor groups, noting increased specialization in specific industry verticals.

Analysis of CVE-2024-23897 Jenkins arbitrary file read vulnerability and its role in supply chain attacks. The vulnerability in the Jenkins CLI args4j library allowed unauthenticated reading of files on the Jenkins controller. Threat actors used this to extract cryptographic keys, build secrets, and credentials, then compromised software build pipelines to inject backdoors into downstream software products.

Analysis of CVE-2024-27198 JetBrains TeamCity authentication bypass vulnerability. The critical flaw allowed unauthenticated attackers to create administrative accounts and execute arbitrary code on TeamCity servers. Multiple threat actors including APT29 exploited the vulnerability within hours of disclosure to compromise CI/CD pipelines, highlighting the ongoing targeting of software supply chain infrastructure by both nation-state and criminal actors.

Campaign analysis of Evil Corp operations following OFAC sanctions evasion through ransomware rebranding. The group cycled through WastedLocker, Hades, Phoenix, PayloadBin, and Macaw Locker variants to distance victims from sanctions implications. Analysis covers the group's access to LockBit affiliate program and the legal challenges victims face when engaging in ransom negotiations with sanctioned entities.

Technical analysis of Windows ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) tampering techniques used to blind security monitoring. Covers patching of EtwEventWrite in ntdll.dll, kernel-level ETW provider disabling via NtTraceControl, and manipulation of ETW session configurations to selectively drop security-relevant events. These techniques are increasingly combined with AMSI bypasses as a prerequisite step before PowerShell-based post-exploitation.

Analysis of FIN8 evolution from point-of-sale targeting to enterprise ransomware operations. The group's transition included adoption of the Sardonic backdoor framework for initial access, White Rabbit ransomware for encryption operations, and eventual affiliation with the ALPHV/BlackCat RaaS program. FIN8 maintains sophisticated capabilities including custom UEFI bootkit development for persistence below the operating system level.

Vulnerability analysis of CVE-2025-24813 Apache Tomcat deserialization remote code execution. The vulnerability allowed attackers to upload serialized Java objects via partial PUT requests to default session persistence storage locations. When combined with a deserialize-capable library on the classpath, attackers achieved remote code execution. Mass exploitation followed within 30 hours of public PoC availability.

Analysis of Citrix Bleed (CVE-2023-4966) exploitation patterns and long-term impact. LockBit, Medusa, and multiple other ransomware groups exploited the vulnerability months after patches were available. Analysis reveals that patching alone was insufficient as session tokens captured before patching remained valid. Organizations required forced session invalidation and credential rotation to fully remediate, a step many missed.

Technical analysis of Kubernetes RBAC misconfiguration exploitation. Covers escalation paths through overly permissive ClusterRoleBindings, abuse of pod creation privileges for node-level access, exploitation of service account token auto-mounting, and lateral movement through cross-namespace network policies. Includes detection strategies using OPA/Gatekeeper audit policies and Kubernetes audit log monitoring.

Campaign analysis of TA577 thread hijacking and HTML smuggling campaigns delivering Pikabot as a QakBot successor. The group intercepted legitimate email threads from compromised mailboxes, injecting replies containing HTML attachments that assembled malicious payloads client-side to bypass email security gateways. Pikabot provided initial access for subsequent ransomware deployment by affiliated groups.

Analysis of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploitation. Research demonstrates that LLM-based agents can autonomously discover and exploit certain classes of web application vulnerabilities including SQL injection, SSRF, and path traversal. Threat actors have begun integrating AI tools into reconnaissance and exploitation workflows, reducing the skill barrier for conducting sophisticated attacks against enterprise web applications.

Analysis of SaaS-to-SaaS supply chain risks in enterprise environments. Threat actors increasingly target the interconnections between SaaS applications, exploiting OAuth integrations, API tokens, and webhook configurations to move between services. Documented attack paths include compromising a marketing automation platform to access CRM data, pivoting from project management tools to cloud storage, and abusing SSO trust to access downstream applications.

Comprehensive analysis of initial access broker (IAB) ecosystem and its role in ransomware operations. IABs on underground forums sell access to compromised networks for prices ranging from $500 to $100,000 depending on victim size and access type. The most common access types sold include VPN credentials (38%), RDP access (27%), web shell access (18%), and compromised cloud accounts (12%). Analysis maps specific IABs to their downstream ransomware affiliate customers.

Profile of FIN12 (Pistol Tempest) rapid ransomware deployment methodology. The group achieves encryption within an average of 48 hours from initial access, significantly faster than the industry average dwell time of 7 days. FIN12 deliberately avoids data exfiltration to reduce detection risk and relies exclusively on initial access brokers, demonstrating the efficiency of specialized roles within the ransomware ecosystem.

Analysis of enterprise risks from LLM integration in customer-facing applications and internal tools. Documented threat scenarios include prompt injection via user input to extract system prompts and API keys, data exfiltration through AI tool-use chains that access databases and send results externally, and manipulation of AI-powered code review tools to approve vulnerable code. Recommends sandboxed execution, output filtering, and human-in-the-loop controls for sensitive AI operations.
